relatedSnapshot.title: Make phone pricing easy to change
relatedSnapshot.description:
## What this does

Lets Acquisity price Twilio and Sendblue separately. Both start with a 20% markup, while platform admins can change future pricing without a code release.

## Done when

* Twilio and Sendblue each start at 20%.
* Platform admins can set a future global percentage for either provider.
* An approved organization-specific percentage overrides only that organization's chosen provider.
* Provider, organization and effective dates cannot leak into another customer's pricing.
* Old charges keep their original pricing and every change has an audit record.
* Non-admin and impersonated sessions cannot change pricing.

## Not included

Customer balances, payments or billing screens.

## Wait for

Nothing.

relatedSnapshot.title: Reps can't call or text because the phone balance check gives up too fast
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Reps in the AI Acquisition Sales Team workspace often can't call or text prospects, so this ticket makes calls and texts go through and helps the team book more meetings. Calls and texts give up almost at once on a shared phone balance lock. The text box's phone number check can also wait forever, and we can't see which slow request held the page up.

## Problem

On 8 Oct 2026 Name 1 couldn't text a client who was waiting for a payment link. Their text box showed "Texting is unavailable. Checking organization phone number" and never cleared, and one text at 10:03 pm Name 3 failed with "Message not sent: phone funding could not be verified". Name 2 Name 2 has heard "your phone balance is being checked" on 10 or more calls a day since 7 Oct. Each of those calls hangs up before it dials the prospect.

## Root cause

There are two separate faults. Every call, text and billing job for the workspace takes one shared balance lock. A rep's call gives up the moment it finds the lock busy, and a text gives up after 200 ms. Separately, the text box's phone number check travels in the same bundled request as the rest of the page, so it waits for the slowest request, and it shows "Texting is unavailable" for the whole wait.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph Today
    A1[Rep calls or texts] --> B1{Balance lock free?}
    B1 -- "busy, about 1 in 7 tries" --> C1[Fails: balance is being checked]
    B1 -- free --> D1[Call or text goes out]
    E1[Text box opens] --> F1[Phone number check bundled with slow page requests] --> G1[Texting is unavailable until the slowest one ends]
  end
  subgraph After
    A2[Rep calls or texts] --> B2{Balance lock free?}
    B2 -- busy --> W2[Wait and retry for up to about 3 s] --> B2
    B2 -- free --> D2[Call or text goes out]
    E2[Text box opens] --> F2[Phone number check sent on its own] --> G2[Ready, or a clear error that retries itself]
  end
```

Calls and texts now wait a few seconds for the lock, and the phone number check no longer waits on other requests.

## Who's affected

The calls and texts that pay from the phone balance run only in the AI Acquisition Sales Team workspace today, so it's one workspace and all its reps. We sampled that workspace's lock read-only on 8 Oct 2026 from 11:18 to 11:21 pm Name 3, a quiet time. It was held in 34 of 240 checks (14%) by 25 different holders. In the 24 hours to 9:40 pm Name 3 on 8 Oct 2026, Sentry counted the call message 20 times (16 users, ACQUISITY-5CF). It counted the text message 17 times (15 users, ACQUISITY-5CW).
 Calls that hang up before dialing leave no call record, so the real number of blocked calls is likely higher than Sentry shows. We don't know which slow request held up Name 100's text box, because there's no recording of the session and the database queries don't say which request sent them. That's why this ticket adds both.

## Proposed fix

* Calls and texts wait and retry on a busy balance lock for up to 2 s, with a short random gap between tries. The hourly call funding check keeps failing fast, because it retries on its own schedule. Every text and the phone number purchase and renewal steps already opted into waiting, so they now wait up to 2 s too.
* The phone number check is sent on its own, not bundled. While it's loading, nothing is blocked, because the server still refuses a call or text without a number, so a slow check can't stop a rep. A failed check shows "We couldn't check your workspace's phone number. Trying again…" in every text box and retries by itself every 10 s, so a half-typed text is never lost to a reload.
* Each database query outside a transaction carries the name of the request that sent it, so PlanetScale shows the slow request by name. Setting `DB_QUERY_TAGS=off` and redeploying turns it off.
* Session recording is on for the sales team workspace only, with inputs masked and network timing captured, but no request or response bodies.

## Out of scope

The background billing jobs that hold the lock most of the time, mainly reconciling settled calls, can be throttled per workspace once we've measured them. If they turn out to dominate, that becomes its own ticket.

## Done when

* A call or text that finds the lock held by another holder for 500 ms waits, then goes through. How to check: a database test holds the lease for 500 ms and admits a call and a text.
* A call or text that finds the lock held past the wait budget still fails with the existing message. How to check: the same test holds it for 5 s.
* The text box never shows "Texting is unavailable" while the phone number check is still loading, and a failed check shows an error in the person, deal and in-call text boxes and retries by itself.
* PlanetScale query stats show the request name on queries from the web app.
* In the week after release, Sentry ACQUISITY-5CF and ACQUISITY-5CW fire at least 80% less often than the 20 and 17 a day counted above.

## Implementation context

* Lock: `account-lock.ts`, call admission in `admission.ts`.
* Request bundling: `trpc/client.tsx`, phone check hook in `record-hooks.ts`.
* Name 4 fix for the same "still checking" mistake on SMS consent: <issue id="<uuid>" href="ENG-14593">ENG-14593</issue>.
* Lock investigation from 7 Oct 2026: <issue id="<uuid>" href="ENG-14909">ENG-14909</issue>.

## Reports

* <issue id="<uuid>" href="ENG-14909">ENG-14909</issue>
* <issue id="<uuid>" href="ENG-14995">ENG-14995</issue>
* <issue id="<uuid>" href="ENG-14962">ENG-14962</issue>
* <issue id="<uuid>" href="ENG-14839">ENG-14839</issue>
* <issue id="<uuid>" href="ENG-14817">ENG-14817</issue>

The phone do-not-contact list from ENG-14346 blocks numbers from calls and texts. Today it can only be managed through the public API (`apps/api/src/routes/v1/dnc-phones.ts`) and workflows. Nobody can see or edit it inside the app.

* tRPC procedures in the web app to list, add and remove blocked numbers. Reuse `packages/db/src/repositories/dnc-phone-repository.ts` and keep the API's permission and normalisation rules.
* A "Do not contact" tab or section on Settings › Phone (the v2 page from ENG-14214), in the settings format:

James asked for this as a follow-up on 2026-09-28, while reviewing PR Acquisity/Acquisity#6580.

relatedSnapshot.title: Reconnect the browser phone line before dialing instead of timing out
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

A rep whose Acquisity tab has been open for a while clicks Call and gets "Call failed: Device registration timeout" until they refresh the page. The dialer should reconnect the browser phone line itself before dialing, keep its token fresh, and report the failure when it cannot.

## Problem

On 10 September Name 5 (AI Acquisition Sales Team) could text but could not call. His tab had been open since the previous evening. The browser's phone connection to Twilio had dropped while the laptop was asleep and its one hour token had expired. When he clicked Call, the dialer noticed the connection was not registered, pushed in a fresh token, then only waited 10 seconds for Twilio to reconnect on its own. It never asked the SDK to re-register, and the SDK's own reconnect backoff can take up to 20 seconds, so the wait lost the race. The attempt never reached Twilio: there is no call record, no Twilio error, and no server-side trace, because browser logs stay in the console.

This became possible when inbound ringing (ENG-12193, Acquisity/Acquisity#5943, merged 12 August) started creating the phone connection at page load and keeping it for the life of the tab. Before that a connection was created per call, so the passive wait added in Acquisity/Acquisity#5677 never mattered. The token refresh for that long-lived connection runs once with no retry, so a single failed refresh (for example waking before Wi-Fi is back) leaves the line dead until something else pushes a token in.

## Proposed fix

When a call starts and the phone line exists but is not registered, rebuild the line from scratch on a fresh connection with the new token, so the call goes through without a page refresh. Keep the token refresh alive by retrying it and by refreshing again after any Twilio authorization error. When a call still cannot start before dialing, record that failure so engineering can see it.

## What's included

* Outbound call start recovers an unregistered or stale phone line automatically.
* Token refresh for the long-lived line retries on failure and re-runs after Twilio auth errors.
* Pre-dial call failures are reported to Sentry with the reason and the SDK state, no personal data.
* Regression tests for the unregistered-line path and the refresh retry.

Not included: the inbound call card, readiness UI and recovery controls, which stay in ENG-13432; any change to call routing, caller ID, permissions or billing.

## How it should work

* If the line is not registered when Call is clicked, the dialer does not try to revive it: it discards the line and builds a new one with the fresh token on a fresh connection, then dials. (Sending anything over a dead connection makes the phone library report an error that the call screen treats as a failed call, which is why reviving it in place does not work.)
* The user-facing error only appears after the rebuild also fails, and it names the real reason rather than a generic timeout.
* The token refresh retries with a short backoff and gives up after a few attempts with a logged error; a later Twilio auth error triggers another refresh.
* Inbound ringing keeps working after recovery: the rebuilt line is registered for incoming calls the same way the original was.
* Recovery must not interrupt an active or ringing call; it only runs when no call is in progress.

## Who can do what

Not applicable: no permission or ownership changes. Existing call permission and calling setup checks are unchanged.

## What the user sees

Clicking Call on a long-open tab connects normally after a short delay. If the line cannot be recovered, the existing "Call failed" toast shows a specific reason and refreshing the page still works as a fallback. No new screens.

## Done when

* A tab whose phone line has become unregistered can place a call without a page refresh.
* A tab whose token expired while the refresh failed once can place a call without a page refresh.
* An active or ringing call is never interrupted by recovery.
* A pre-dial failure appears in Sentry with the SDK state and reason.
* Unit tests cover the unregistered-line recovery, the rebuild path, and the refresh retry.

## Open questions

None: all required decisions are settled.

## Expected outcome

Reps stop hitting "Device registration timeout" on tabs left open, and any remaining pre-dial failure is visible to engineering instead of only in the rep's toast.

## Implementation context

AI context.md

relatedSnapshot.title: Contact record DNC checkbox ignores phone blocks, so phone-only people can't be unblocked from the UI
relatedSnapshot.description:
**Summary** The Do Not Contact checkbox on a person's record only looks at emails. A person with only a phone number can be blocked for calls and texts through the phone block list added in ENG-14346 (#6648). Their record still shows them as not blocked, the checkbox is disabled, and the UI has no way to remove the block.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Go to CRM → People and create a person with a phone number and no email, e.g. `<phone>`.
2. Block that number with the **Add Phone to DNC** workflow step (or `POST /v1/workspaces/{id}/dnc/phones`).
3. Open the person's record.
4. Try to call or text them.
5. Hover over the **Do Not Contact** checkbox.

**Expected**

* The checkbox shows the person as blocked, because their phone number is on the list.
* A user with DNC permission can untick it to remove the number from the list, the same way it works for emails.
* For a person with no email, the checkbox can still add their phone numbers to the list.

**Actual**

* Calls and texts are refused: *"Remove the number from the do-not-contact list before calling."*
* The checkbox is unchecked and disabled.
* The tooltip says *"Add an email to this contact to enable DNC"*, even though the person is already blocked.
* There's no way to unblock from the UI. It can only be done with the **Remove Phone from DNC** workflow step or the API.

Proof : <url:jam.dev>

relatedSnapshot.title: Play a ringing tone while an outbound call rings
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Play a normal ringing tone to the rep while an outbound call rings, when the carrier sends no ringing sound of its own. Reps on Name 6 and the sales team hear silence until the person answers, so they can't tell whether a call is ringing and may hang up early, which costs connected calls.

## Problem

A rep clicks call in the dialler or the power dialler. On most calls they hear nothing until the person picks up, and then the person is suddenly there. They expected to hear ringing, as they did on their previous phone system. It's been reported in #app-acquisity-crm on 13 and 14 Oct 2026 and in ENG-14910.

## Root cause

We connect the rep only when the person answers, so while it rings the rep hears only what the person's carrier sends. Many US carriers send no ringing sound, and the browser never plays one of its own.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Rep clicks call] --> B[Twilio dials the person]
  B --> C[Call is ringing]
  C -- carrier sends sound --> D[Rep hears ringing]
  C -- no sound --> E[NEW: browser plays ringing tone]
  E --> F[Stops on answer or hang-up]
```

Look at the "no sound" branch, which is silent today and plays a tone after this change.

## Proposed fix

* When the browser phone reports ringing and says the carrier sends no sound, play a looping US ringing tone through the rep's chosen speaker.
* Stop it when the call is answered, ends, fails or is cancelled.
* Play nothing when the carrier already sends a ringing sound, so the rep never hears two.

## Out of scope

The rest of ENG-15157, which times each step of a call and rewrites call error messages. This ticket ships only its ringing tone.

## Done when

* A unit test fires ringing with no carrier sound, then answer, and the tone starts and then stops.
* With carrier sound, the tone never starts, and a later ringing event with carrier sound stops a tone that's playing.
* Repeated ringing events never play two tones at once.
* On a preview, a call to a real phone that rings without answering plays the tone until hang-up.

## Implementation context

* Call start: `Device.connect` in `apps/web/hooks/use-twilio-device.tsx` (about line 553). Dial TwiML sets `answerOnBridge` in `apps/web/app/api/voice/answer/route.ts` line 168.
* Ringing is handled for UI state only in `apps/web/lib/voice/attach-call-listeners.ts`. The Voice SDK `ringing` event passes `hasEarlyMedia`.
* A WebAudio tone already exists for incoming calls in `apps/web/components/crm/call/incoming/use-incoming-ringtone.ts`. Output device handling is in `apps/web/lib/voice/apply-stored-audio-settings.ts`.

Ring a rep's own phone for incoming calls
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

When a rep has forwarding on, incoming calls to their CRM number also ring their own phone: at the same time as the browser, after it, or instead of it. The rep must press 1 before the caller is connected, so their phone's own voicemail can never swallow a call. Nothing changes for anyone until the settings in the next ticket let a rep turn forwarding on.

## Problem

Incoming calls can only ring the browser, and there is nowhere to store a forwarding choice. A phone's own voicemail also looks like a real answer to Twilio, so simply dialling a mobile would log unanswered calls as answered and lose voicemails outside the CRM.

## What's included

* Stored forwarding settings for each rep and a workspace setting that allows forwarding.
* Routing for the three modes, the "press 1" screen, and logging calls answered on the phone.
* Tests.
* Recording, the settings screens and the balance check are separate tickets.

## Blocked by

None: can start immediately.

## How it should work

* Each rep's settings in each workspace store a forwarding number, when and how it was verified, a mode (off, ring both at once, browser first then phone, or phone only) and a browser ring time (10, 15, 20 or 30 seconds, default 15). Forwarding is off by default. Each workspace has a setting that allows forwarding, on by default.
* The phone rings only if, at the moment the call arrives, the assigned rep has forwarding on, their number is verified, and the workspace allows forwarding. Otherwise the call behaves exactly as today.
* **Ring both at once:** the browser and the phone ring together for 20 seconds. Answering in the browser stops the phone; accepting on the phone stops the browser. If the phone is switched off, its voicemail may answer first and end the browser ring, and the caller gets the CRM voicemail.
* **Browser first:** the browser rings for the rep's chosen time, then the phone rings for 20 seconds.
* **Phone only:** the phone rings for 20 seconds straight away.
* The phone shows the caller's real number. No caller ID override is set, which is the path Twilio supports going forward.
* The rep hears a short prompt and has about 8 seconds to press 1. Any other key, silence, or the phone's own voicemail ends the forwarded ring and the caller hears the CRM voicemail.
* A call counts as answered on the phone only when the rep pressed 1. Twilio's own answered status is not trusted for the phone. The key press only counts from a verified Twilio request, for a call we actually forwarded, once. If it cannot be saved, the forwarded ring ends and the caller gets voicemail, so a connected call is never logged as missed.
* A call accepted on the phone is logged exactly like a browser answer: answered, talk time, contact and deal links, counted as a connect. A declined or unanswered forward is logged as missed and any voicemail is saved as today.
* Repeated Twilio callbacks never ring the phone twice.
* Premium-rate and shared-cost numbers cannot be used. A call Twilio refuses to connect because of a country or fraud rule goes to voicemail and is logged with its reason.
* No phone numbers or names are put in webhook URLs or logs.

## Who can do what

* Forwarding only goes to the number stored on that rep's own settings in that workspace.
* A removed or banned rep never has calls forwarded.

## Done when

* With forwarding off, incoming calls behave exactly as today.
* In a preview, with a real mobile, in every mode: pressing 1 connects and logs an answered call with talk time; not pressing, declining, or the phone being off sends the caller to CRM voicemail and logs a missed call; in ring-both mode, answering in the browser logs a browser answer.
* The same checks pass for a workspace on its own Twilio subaccount.
* Automated tests cover each mode, browser versus phone answers, accepted versus not accepted when Twilio reports the call as completed, duplicate callbacks, an unverified number, a failed key-press save, and a number Twilio refuses.
* High-risk country permissions are confirmed off on our main Twilio account.
* The database change is additive only.

## Implementation context

* High-risk: live call routing, database change, and a paid outbound call leg with no balance check until the billing ticket for forwarded calls lands.
* Twilio does not document the status it reports when the "press 1" screen hangs up, which is why acceptance is recorded by us.
* Talk time for phone answers includes the few seconds of the prompt.
* Call flow, code map, Twilio references and test matrix: AI context.md.

relatedSnapshot.title: Stop showing "Texting is unavailable" while the text box is still checking
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

When a rep opens the text box on a person or deal, they sometimes see a red "Texting is unavailable. SMS is unavailable while consent status cannot be verified. Try again shortly." notice that disappears by itself. Nothing is actually wrong: the app is still checking whether the person accepts texts. This ticket shows that wait as a wait, and keeps the red notice for real problems, with a way to retry.

## Problem

Reported on the 30 Sep migration call: the notice showed for up to a minute on load, then went away. It looked like texting was broken during the busiest week of the move from Close.

Checked on main on 1 Oct: the text box treats "still checking" and "the check failed" as the same thing and shows the outage wording for both. The check retries quietly three times, so when the database is slow (the Close import was running) the wait, and the red notice, can last close to a minute. So this is not only a side effect of the import. Any slow moment shows a false outage.

The same wording also appears when retrying can never help, for example when the person was deleted or the rep is not allowed to see them.

## User experience

* **Checking:** the text box is disabled and says "Checking whether you can text this person…". No red notice. Sending stays blocked until the check finishes.
* **Check failed:** a notice says "We couldn't check whether this person accepts texts." with a Retry button. It no longer says "try again shortly" with nothing to press.
* **Not allowed or not found:** the notice says the rep cannot text this person, with no Retry.
* **Opted out or do not contact:** unchanged, these already have their own clear messages.

This applies to the text box on person and deal records (page and drawer), the in-call text box, and the first-text box in Conversations. The reply box in Conversations already behaves correctly.

## What's included

* The loading, failed and not-allowed states above on every surface that shows the notice today.
* Sending stays blocked while the answer is unknown. A text must never go out before the consent check has passed.
* Fewer silent retries, so a real failure shows within seconds instead of after a minute.
* Not included: making the consent check itself faster. It runs several database reads each time the box opens. If the notice still appears often after this change, that is a separate performance ticket.

## Done when

- [ ] With the consent check held open, the text box shows the checking state and no red notice, and Send is disabled.
- [ ] With the check failing, the notice offers Retry, and Retry re-runs the check and recovers when it succeeds.
- [ ] A person the rep cannot access, or a deleted person, shows a "cannot text this person" message without Retry and without "try again shortly".
- [ ] Opted-out and do-not-contact messages are unchanged.
- [ ] No text can be sent while the check is loading or failed.
- [ ] Browser QA covers a person page, a person drawer, a deal and the Conversations first-text box with the request blocked and then restored.

## Implementation context

* The cause is in `apps/web/hooks/use-contact-sms-consent.ts` (about lines 62 to 73): `consentUnavailableReason` returns the outage message for `isError || isPending`. The sibling `actionDisabledReason` in the same hook already separates the two ("Checking SMS consent").
* Rendered by `TextBlockedNotice` in `apps/web/components/crm-v2/record/record-composer.tsx` and by the first-text body in `apps/web/components/crm-v2/conversations/composer-text.tsx`. The Conversations reply notice in the same file already has a Retry pattern to copy.
* The query has no retry override, so the default three retries with back-off apply. The text box is mounted hidden from page load, so the check is often mid-retry when the rep opens Text.
* Several callers read `consentUnavailableReason` (`use-contact-sms-composer.ts`, the legacy Calls and Texts tab). Review them together when its meaning changes.
* Tests that pin today's behaviour and need updating: `tests/hooks/use-contact-sms-consent.test.tsx` and `tests/components/crm-v2/record/record-composer.test.tsx`.
* Not verified: the exact duration on 30 Sep. The one minute figure fits three slow attempts plus back-off but was not reproduced.

relatedSnapshot.title: Allow call forwarding when phone wallet billing is disabled
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Problem

Incoming calls configured to ring the browser and a verified mobile fall back to browser-only ringing when Name 7 is disabled. Forwarding admission currently treats the disabled billing feature as a funding failure.

## Expected behavior

* Phone Calling controls access to mobile forwarding.
* With Phone Calling enabled and Name 7 disabled, forwarding skips wallet admission even for workspaces already enrolled in Twilio billing. This exception applies only to forwarding; existing outbound-call and messaging funding behavior is unchanged.
* With both features enabled, existing funding checks and wallet settlement apply.
* With Phone Calling disabled, mobile forwarding is unavailable.
* Preserve verified destinations, workspace forwarding permission, webhook signature verification, press-1 acceptance, and CRM outcomes.

## Acceptance criteria

Cover simultaneous, after-browser, and phone-only modes; verify the feature combinations and that funded calls retain funding deadlines, denial behavior, and settlement protections. Keep the fix scoped; no database migration is expected.

## Local implementation

Implemented on `feature/eng-14207-allow-call-forwarding-when-phone-wallet-billing-is-disabled`, based on main. Committed and pushed as `fb0ffbdcf3`. Ready-for-review PR: Acquisity/Acquisity#6569, targeting main.

Forwarding checks Phone Calling before dialing. When Phone Wallet Top-ups is disabled, it skips creating a funding deadline and wallet admission, including for enrolled workspaces. Existing active funding attempts cannot be bypassed. Other call and messaging funding policies remain unchanged.

Validation: focused forwarding tests and Biome checks pass. Typecheck is blocked by the existing invitation code being unable to resolve the installed `<mention>/core/context` dependency; no errors reported in changed files.

relatedSnapshot.title: Turn on phone billing safely with automatic settlement setup
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Make phone billing turn on in one safe, approved step, so a billing setting can never stop a sales team from texting again. On 6 Oct 2026 the AI Acquisition Sales Team couldn't send texts for about two hours. Name 7 had started putting wallet money on hold for each text, and nothing was set up to finalise those holds. This programme stops expired holds from blocking a whole account and lets a workspace take new holds only when it's enrolled in settlement. Then it makes enrolment automatic, before ENG-14796 turns billing on for every Phone Calling workspace.

## Problem

Three things decide whether a workspace is billed today, and they don't agree. Texts and calls take a hold when Phone Calling and Name 7 are both on, or when the workspace has a settlement setup whose charging start has passed. Number renewals, number purchases and SMS registration fees look only at the two flags. Name 8 a hold needs the settlement setup and also Name 7. An admin creates the settlement setup by hand, in Admin, Workspaces, the row menu, Twilio billing.

A text hold lasts 23 hours. A hold that nothing finalises stays unresolved. Once it's within a minute of running out, a safety check refuses every new text, renewal, number purchase and SMS registration fee on that billing account. Users see "phone funding could not be verified. Please try again shortly", which retrying can't fix.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Text or call sent] --> B[2: hold only if enrolled]
  B --> C[Settlement finalises hold]
  B -- not finalised --> D[1: reconcile expired hold]
  D --> E[Account keeps working]
  F[3: automatic enrolment] --> C
```

The numbers show where each child changes the path. ENG-14810 (1) reconciles expired holds instead of leaving them to block the account. ENG-14811 (2) stops new holds when nothing can finalise them, and ENG-14812 (3) enrols workspaces automatically.

Incident evidence from the read-only production replica (not code-verified): the switch went on at 12:41 pm UTC on 5 Oct 2026. 117 texts sent with holds and none was finalised. The first holds ran out at 12:20 pm UTC on 6 Oct, and every text failed until we closed 121 old holds by hand at 2:33 pm UTC. Texts sent with holds finalised from 2:39 pm UTC.

## User experience

A workspace with phone billing just keeps working. If billing needs attention, users see a message that says what's wrong and who can fix it, and an admin sees the held items in the Twilio billing panel. A workspace that isn't enrolled in settlement keeps texting and calling without holds.

## What's included

1. ENG-14810: expired holds are reconciled against Autumn and Twilio evidence and closed only when no money can still move. Anything unclear goes to a review state that admins can see, and the error message says what's actually wrong.
2. ENG-14811: new holds start only when the workspace is enrolled in settlement. Work already paid for or reserved still finishes.
3. ENG-14812: approved workspaces are enrolled in settlement automatically, in safe stages, and blocked ones show the reason.

## Out of scope

* One settlement setup per billing account instead of per workspace. It changes about 25 call sites and the table keys, and 7 of the 329 workspaces with Phone Calling share a billing account (production replica, 6 Oct 2026). ENG-14812 leaves those 7 unenrolled with a warning.
* Removing the Name 7 flag and its remaining checks, which ENG-14796 owns.
* Sendblue billing, which ENG-12622 owns.
* Customer notices and the go-live approval, which ENG-12727 owns.

## Execution order

1. ENG-14810 and ENG-14811: start now, in parallel.
2. ENG-14796: merges after ENG-14811.
3. ENG-14812: after ENG-14810 and ENG-14811, and its production enrolment waits for the ENG-12727 approval.

## Decisions needed

* **Does an admin turning on Phone Calling for a workspace count as the production approval that** ENG-12727 **asks for?** Recommended: yes, when an admin turns it on for that workspace, because James wants billing to be automatic and the admin's action is recorded with their name. Partner-level enablement doesn't count until decided separately. Decider: James Keeble. Blocks: ENG-14812's production enrolment only.

## Name 9 and rollback

ENG-14810 and ENG-14811 ship behind the existing billing switches. ENG-14812 runs in report-only mode on production first, and the report is posted on ENG-14796 before any enrolment. A charging start date can't be removed, so undoing enrolment is a forward procedure. Stop new billed activity for the workspace through ENG-14811's enrolment check. Settlement, wallet-change recovery and cost reconciliation keep running for everything already held or owed. Don't pause "Charge verified usage" as a rollback, because that also stops settling existing liabilities. Never delete settlement records or forgive amounts due as a rollback step.

## Done when

* An expired hold can no longer block a billing account unless its provider outcome is truly unresolved, and those cases show in the Twilio billing panel.
* No path starts a new hold for a workspace that isn't enrolled in settlement.
* Approved workspaces are enrolled automatically, and the report lists every skipped workspace with its reason.
* ENG-14796 is unblocked.

## Implementation context

* Safety check: `assertNoExpiredPhoneFunding` in unsettled-funding.ts
* Manual setup: `configureTwilioBilling` in operations.ts
* Manual repair on 6 Oct 2026: 121 text holds (117 accepted, 4 unknown, all created before the 2:23 pm UTC charging start) were set to `settled` with a note. Settlement only rates costs incurred after the charging start, so these won't be charged. ENG-14810 reconciles each of them into its new closed or needs-review state, so `settled` keeps meaning "collected".
* Full research and evidence: AI context.md

relatedSnapshot.title: Reps' calls fail or hang up when billing jobs hold the phone balance lock
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Reps' calls still fail, or get hung up before the prospect's phone rings, when a background billing job holds the workspace's phone balance lock. Fixing it means every dial reaches a prospect, so reps make more calls and book more meetings. From 6 to 9 Oct 2026 our server hung up 74 sales-team calls this way, and the 9 Oct fix in ENG-14996 didn't stop it. This ticket stops a busy lock from ever blocking a rep's call.

## Problem

An SDR in the AI Acquisition Sales Team workspace reported on 10 Oct 2026 that "every 5 or so calls" a popup said they were out of credits and to try again later, and that calls "randomly hang up". We think both are this bug, seen at two steps:

* At the start of a call, the browser asks for a call token. If the lock is busy, the rep sees a popup: "Your phone balance is being checked. Please try again shortly." Reps read this as being out of credits.
* When Twilio connects the rep, it asks our answer webhook what to do. If the lock is still busy there, our server speaks the same sentence and hangs up. The rep hears about 5 seconds of message, then silence, and has to dial again.

The webhook returns HTTP 200, so these hang-ups never reach Sentry or Twilio's error log. 75 of the 76 we found also left a CRM call event stuck at "pending" with no call row, so the attempt is missing from the person's timeline.

## Root cause

Every call, text and billing job in the workspace shares one phone balance lock. A call checks funding twice, once for the token and once at the answer webhook, and each check needs the lock. Since 9 Oct a call waits up to 2 seconds for it. But the settlement job holds the lock for 1.6 seconds at the median and 3.1 seconds at p99 (max 9.8 seconds), and the rating job took it 108,373 times from 6 to 11 Oct. So at busy times the 2 second wait runs out and the call still fails.

Today:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Rep clicks call] --> B[Token: funding check takes lock]
  B -- busy over 2 s --> X[Name 10: balance being checked]
  B --> C[Answer webhook: funding check takes lock]
  C -- busy over 2 s --> Y[Speak message and hang up]
  C --> D[Dial prospect]
```

After this change:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Rep clicks call] --> B[CHANGED: one balance read, no lock]
  B --> C[CHANGED: admit call, settle later]
  C --> D[Dial prospect]
  E[Billing jobs] --> F[CHANGED: short lock holds only]
```

The rep's call no longer waits on, or fails because of, a lock that a background job holds.

## Who's affected

Only the AI Acquisition Sales Team workspace pays for calls from the phone balance today, so it's one workspace and all its reps. From our answer-webhook logs, calls hung up by the balance message per Name 3 day were 9 on 6 Oct, 24 on 7 Oct, 35 on 8 Oct and 6 on 9 Oct, which is 4.1% of browser calls from 5 to 9 Oct and up to 10% on the worst days. 12 of 30 reps hit it, one of them 30 times. After the fix went live on 9 Oct at 1:24 pm Name 3, 7 more busy failures hit reps that evening. The weekend since had only 76 calls, so we can't yet say how often it happens now at weekday volume. We haven't matched a failure to the SDR who reported it, because the report doesn't name them.

## Proposed fix

* Check the balance once per call with a read that doesn't take the lock. Only steps that move money take it.
* At the answer webhook, never hang up a call because the lock is busy. Admit it and settle the cost afterwards (see Decisions needed).
* Make the settlement and rating jobs hold the lock only around the write, not across whole-workspace work, so a rep's step rarely waits.
* Log every funding denial at the webhook to Sentry, and write the call row even when admission fails, so the attempt shows on the timeline.
* If a call still can't start, show a plain message that says it's temporary and isn't about credits.

## How it should work

* A real low balance still blocks a call, with the existing "balance is too low" message. Only a busy lock stops blocking.
* A call admitted while the lock was busy is settled by the next settlement run, and its cost is never lost. If settlement then finds the balance negative, the existing recharge or hold rules apply.
* Retries stay on the jobs' own schedule. A rep's call never retries for longer than Twilio's 15 second webhook limit.

## Who can do what

Nothing changes in who can call. Reps with calling access keep it. Only billing jobs and the money-moving step write to the phone balance.

## Name 9 and rollback

This changes billing admission, so release it behind a flag for the sales workspace first. Watch one weekday evening (5 to 11 pm Name 3) for busy failures and for any call admitted without a later settlement. Rolling back the flag returns to today's behaviour, and calls admitted during the rollout still settle normally.

## Decisions needed

* **When the lock is busy at the answer webhook, should we let the call through and settle later, or wait longer?** Recommended: let it through and settle later, because a lost dial costs more than one call's charge, and the settlement job already reconciles every call. Decider: the billing owner. Blocks: the webhook change.

## Done when

* A call placed while another holder keeps the lock for 5 seconds goes through, and its cost is settled afterwards. How to check: a database test holds the lock for 5 s and places a call.
* A call with a genuinely low balance is still refused with the low-balance message.
* The answer webhook writes a call row and a Sentry event for every funding denial.
* On a weekday evening after release, our logs show 0 calls hung up by the balance message, against 24 to 35 a day on 7 and 8 Oct.

## Implementation context

* Lock and wait budget: `account-lock.ts`, admission in `admission.ts`, the message in `errors.ts`.
* Token check: `voice.ts` line 639. Answer webhook admission and spoken hang-up: `answer/route.ts` lines 240 and 292 to 312.
* Whole-workspace settlement inside the lock: `funded-call.ts` line 130.
* Lock hold times by holder, 6 to 11 Oct: settle p50 1.6 s, p99 3.1 s, max 9.8 s (1,115 holds); rating 108,373 holds; call admission p50 about 1 s. Source: Axiom "Phone funding account operation finished".
* Prior fix: Acquisity/Acquisity#6994.

## Reports

* ENG-14909
* ENG-14995
* ENG-15076
* SDR feedback relayed by the sales manager in Slack, 10 Oct 2026 at 3:15 pm Name 3.

relatedSnapshot.title: Forward incoming calls to a rep's own phone
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Reps can only answer calls to their CRM number in the browser, so calls they miss away from their desk go to voicemail. This lets a rep add their own phone, choose when it rings, and remove it at any time, while every call, recording and voicemail still lands in the CRM.

## Problem

Reps step away, work from their phone or close the tab, and calls from prospects go straight to voicemail.

## User experience

1. In the phone settings, a rep adds their phone and confirms it is theirs with a code sent by text or by a phone call.
2. They choose **Ring both at once**, **Ring my browser first, then my phone** (after 10, 15, 20 or 30 seconds) or **Ring my phone only**.
3. When the phone rings it shows the caller's real number. On answering, the rep hears "You have a call on your {workspace} line. Press 1 to accept."
4. Pressing 1 connects the call. If they do not press 1, or their phone's own voicemail answers, the caller goes to the CRM voicemail.
5. The call is logged and recorded in the CRM like any other answered call.
6. The rep can remove their phone at any time. An admin can remove it for them, or turn forwarding off for the whole workspace.

## What's included

* Call routing for all three modes.
* The settings, verification and removal for reps and admins.
* Recording every answered incoming call.
* The balance check for forwarded calls is owned by the calls and texting billing programme (Add Billing for calls and texting), not by this master.

## Execution order

Use the lowest-numbered eligible ticket first. Tickets grouped as parallel may start together when there is capacity, but they keep the priority order below. Waves show the earliest dependency unlock, not a barrier.

### Wave 1: can start now

Parallel: none.

1. Ring a rep's own phone for incoming calls: all three ring modes, the "press 1" screen and correct logging. Dormant until the settings ship.

### Wave 2: starts when ticket 1 is done

Parallel: Let reps add, verify and remove a forwarding phone and Record every answered incoming call.

2. Let reps add, verify and remove a forwarding phone: blocked by Ring a rep's own phone for incoming calls. This is when users get the feature.
3. Record every answered incoming call: blocked by Ring a rep's own phone for incoming calls.

Cross-wave overlap: none verified.

Outside this master: Check funds before forwarding a call to a rep's phone sits under the billing programme. It starts when ticket 1 and Check funds before starting Twilio calls are done, and may overlap tickets 2 and 3. Forwarding does not wait for it.

## Done when

* All children are done, and a rep has taken a real forwarded call in production that was logged and recorded correctly.
* Call forwarding activation events are verified landing in PostHog.

## Not included

* Forwarding to another rep or team (see Add blind call transfer).
* Business-hours schedules.
* The missed-call inbox (Show reps their missed calls and voicemails).
* Charging customers for minutes.

relatedSnapshot.title: Let reps pick a call outcome while detection is still finalizing
relatedSnapshot.description:
## What's happening

After a call ends, the wrap-up card shows "Finalizing the detected outcome…" and every outcome button (Answered, No answer, Busy, Left voicemail, Wrong number) is disabled. While it's loading the rep can't click anything — Name 11 had it stuck for over 60 seconds today, though not every time.

## What should happen

The outcome buttons should stay clickable while detection finalizes. The rep picks an outcome and presses **Save outcome**, and their choice wins over the detected one.

## Who it hits and how bad

Reps wrapping up calls, especially in the Power Dialer — it stalls the wrap-up and delays the next call. Reported by Name 11 in #app-acquisity-crm (screenshot attached there).

## How to see it

1. End a call so the wrap-up card appears while "Finalizing the detected outcome…" is still showing (answer detection pending).
2. Try to click an outcome — every choice is disabled until detection resolves, which can take tens of seconds.

## What we know so far

The outcome choices are disabled while outcome resolution is pending, even though saving only needs the call's provider ID, which is already present. Detection polling retries for \~30s+, which is why the buttons stay frozen.

## Done when

- [ ] While "Finalizing the detected outcome…" shows, the rep can pick an outcome and press **Save outcome**; the picked outcome is saved and wins over detection.
- [ ] A test covers picking an outcome during resolution.

<details><summary>For whoever fixes it</summary>

* `apps/web/components/crm-v2/phone/outcome-choices.tsx` — `ChoiceGroup disabled={disabled || call.isResolvingOutcome}` is what greys out the buttons in the wrap-up dock.
* `apps/web/components/crm/call/call-outcome-picker.tsx` — same `call.isResolvingOutcome` disable in `CallOutcomeOptions` for the other picker surface.
* `isResolvingOutcome` is driven by answer-detection polling in `apps/web/components/crm/call/use-completed-call-controller.ts` (retries up to \~30s+).
* `canPickCallOutcome` only requires `callSid !== null`, and `confirmOutcome` writes via `updateCallOutcome` keyed on `callSid`, so a manual pick can already be saved during detection.
* Thread: <url:acquisityworkspace.slack.com>
  </details>

relatedSnapshot.title: Always save a person's phone number: normalise it, never reject it
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

A person is always saved with the phone number they gave, from a workflow or the API. Acquisity normalises the number when it can and keeps it as typed when it can't. A phone number never stops a person from being created or updated.

## Problem

Since Acquisity/Acquisity#6663 (merged 30 Sep, ENG-14343), the workflow person step refuses the whole write with "phone must be a valid phone number" when the phone fails strict validation. ENG-14343 asked for phones to be normalised and matched "in any common format". It did not ask for numbers to be rejected; that was added during review in commit `82e4dbbc7a` ("validate phones before workflow writes").

What it cost in the AI Acquisition Sales Team workspace between 30 Sep and 2 Oct:

* 40 workflow runs failed across three workflows (website and Fast-Track intake, webinar sign-up, lead tool result).
* 17 website sign-ups were not created at all, even though each had a valid email. Others were not updated.
* The workflows have been changed to check the phone first and leave it off when it is rejected, and the 40 runs were replayed. Nobody is missing now, but 19 people are saved without their phone.
* Of those 19 numbers, 16 are the right length for a US number but fail the strict check. 3 are too short (8 or 9 digits).

Forms get typos, test numbers and numbers typed without a country code. Losing the lead, or their number, over that is worse than storing an imperfect number.

## What's included

* `crm/upsert-contact`, `crm/update-contact` and the shared contact write helpers never fail because of the phone.
* A valid number is saved in E.164, as today.
* A number that is the right length but not strictly valid is still normalised and saved.
* A number that can't be normalised is saved as typed and marked unverified, so the app can show it and a rep can fix it.
* Matching keeps working: a number that can't be normalised matches only on its exact typed form.
* Calls and texts keep their own checks. An unverified number can't be dialled or texted until it is fixed, and the app says why.
* The same rule applies to the public API person routes that use the shared write path.
* The run's error message names the step that stopped it, not an earlier "not found" that was carried past. Today these runs show "Contact not found" when the real error is the phone.

## Done when

- [ ] A workflow run with a valid email and the phone `12345678` creates the person with that phone stored, and the run succeeds.
- [ ] A 10-digit US-shaped number that fails strict validation is stored in E.164 and the run succeeds.
- [ ] `+44 7700 900123` and `<phone>` are still stored and matched as today.
- [ ] Texting or calling an unverified number is refused with a clear message, and no other behaviour of the dial and send gates changes.
- [ ] A failed run shows the error from the step that stopped it.
- [ ] Workflows saved before this change behave the same for valid phones.

## Open questions

* How to mark an unverified number. Recommended default: a flag on the phone row, shown as a small "check this number" hint on the person, with no new settings.
* Whether Find person should return "not found" for a number that can't be normalised, where it returns an error today. Recommended default: "not found", so workflows can branch on it.

## Implementation context

* The rejection sits in `apps/web/plugins/workflows/crm/steps/upsert-contact.ts` (three places that return "phone must be a valid phone number") and in `setPrimaryContactPhone` in `apps/web/plugins/workflows/crm/steps/contact-write-utils.ts`, which throws. The normaliser is `packages/db/src/phone-number-normalization.ts` (`normalizeE164PhoneNumber` returns null for anything not valid).
* `matchCrmPersonIdentity` returns `invalid_identity` for such a phone, which `crm/find-person` turns into a step error.
* After this ships, the 19 phones can be filled by replaying the saved run inputs. They are kept in the workflow run history for workflows `bc1d2fbf`, `db110a33` and `df1b25d6`. The build session for the Close automations move will do the replay.
* High-risk path: phone identity and the dial and send gates share this normaliser.
